error_locked: Too many failed attempts. Please wait 15 minutes.
error_expired: Form expired. Please reload the page.
twofa_hint: Code from your authenticator app, or a backup code.
err_not_configured: Machine credentials are missing in the add-on options.
err_bad_url: The LAPI address is not an http(s) address.
err_http_error: The LAPI answered with an error.
err_bad_response: The LAPI answer could not be read.
err_csrf: Request rejected. Please reload the page.
err_internal: Internal error. Check the add-on log.
err_bad_country: Not a valid country code (two letters).
err_no_filter: No filter given — that would delete everything.
nb_reason_hint: Shown as the alert message. Optional.
nb_origin_note: Decisions are created with origin cscli so every bouncer accepts them. CrowdPanel names itself in the scenario text.
al_none: No alerts in the selected period.
chk_allowed: On an allowlist — decisions do not apply.
set_2fa_scan: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.
set_2fa_no_qr: QR generation unavailable — enter the secret by hand.
set_2fa_backup_hint: Each code works once. Write them down now — they are not shown again.
set_2fa_ingress_note: Applies to the direct port only. Through the Home Assistant sidebar, Home Assistant signs you in.
setup_hint: Create a machine account in CrowdSec and copy the credentials into the add-on options. The exact commands are in the add-on documentation.
truncated_hint: Only the first {n} rows are shown — narrow the filter.
too_many: Too many entries to lift. At most {max} at a time — narrow the filter.
err_unsupported_filter: There is no bulk filter for country and network — unban from the row.
wl_hint: Whitelists are YAML files and act while the log is being read — a line from a listed address raises no alert at all. Allowlists instead live in the CrowdSec database and prevent the decision. CrowdPanel only displays whitelists; changing them stays with cscli and an editor.
wl_unavailable: The whitelist parser directory was not found. Set the path in the whitelist_dir option.
aw_hint: Allowlists exempt addresses from decisions. They are created and maintained with cscli allowlists.
ban_not_ip: Only single addresses and ranges can be banned from here.
set_sensors_hint: CrowdPanel reports active decisions, its own decisions and detections of the last 24 hours as sensors to Home Assistant. Switch off with the ha_sensors option.
hub_hint: What CrowdSec has loaded, read from the configuration directory — the same list cscli hub list reports. Versions and update hints are deliberately absent: cscli derives those from the hub index, which lives inside the CrowdSec container, not in the shared directory.
hub_unavailable: CrowdSec configuration directory not found. Set the path in the crowdsec_dir option.
b_unavailable: CrowdSec database not found — set the path with the crowdsec_db option.
b_auto_hint: Created automatically because the same key was used from another address. Pulls nothing itself and can only be deleted together with its parent bouncer.
b_no_agent_hint: Only agents send heartbeats — the part of CrowdSec that processes logs. An account that merely uses the API leaves this empty for good.
m_hint: Everything on this page is read straight from CrowdSec's Prometheus endpoint — the same source cscli metrics builds its tables from. Counters run since CrowdSec started and reset on a restart.
m_enable_hint: By default CrowdSec serves the counters on 127.0.0.1 only, so another add-on cannot reach them. This is not an add-on option — the line lives in CrowdSec's own file /config/.storage/crowdsec/config/config.yaml, where the prometheus section already exists. From the CrowdSec add-on's web terminal: yq eval -i '.prometheus.listen_addr = "0.0.0.0"' /config/.storage/crowdsec/config/config.yaml — then restart the CrowdSec add-on. A different address goes into the option “CrowdSec Prometheus address”.
m_none: CrowdSec reports nothing for this section.
arc_hint: CrowdSec clears out its database after a few weeks. The archive records every detection once, so history, map and alert list reach further back than CrowdSec's own retention — and answer faster. Active decisions, bouncers and metrics still come live from the LAPI.
arc_broken: unusable — history comes from the LAPI
map_no_geoip: Detections are coming in, but not one of them carries coordinates. In CrowdSec they come from the parser crowdsecurity/geoip-enrich in stage s02-enrich — install it with “cscli parsers install crowdsecurity/geoip-enrich” and restart CrowdSec. Without it only the country breakdown remains.
map_zoom_hint: Mouse wheel or two-finger gesture zooms, drag pans, double-click resets.
map_no_outline: The world map could not be loaded.
